tasks.title: Front motor load with an offset CG
tasks.solution: Moment balance: 2·T_f·x_f = 2·T_r·x_r, and the sum 2·T_f + 2·T_r = m. Hence T_f = m·x_r / (2·(x_f + x_r)). The pair closer to the CG carries more; the PX4 pseudo-inverse gives the same split right away.

tasks.title: Yaw gain from tilting the motors
tasks.solution: Mz = CT·(r·sinθ + KM·cosθ), while for a vertical motor Mz = CT·KM. The ratio is (r·sinθ + KM·cosθ)/KM. The vertical thrust drops as cosθ. The PX4 normalization keeps the command, so the yaw loop gain grows by the same factor.

tasks.title: Hexacopter motor load after a failure
tasks.solution: Four motors carry the whole weight: T = m/4 per motor, the fraction is m/(4·T_max)·100 %. Before the failure it was m/6, so the load has grown 1.5 times. The closer the result is to 100 %, the less is left for control.

tasks.title: Axis squeeze in the Betaflight LEGACY mixer
tasks.solution: motorMixRange = max − min. If the span is larger than 1, all three axes are multiplied by 1/span (applyMixerAdjustment); otherwise they stay as they are. Then the throttle is shifted so that the outputs fit into the range.
